in_english.name: Mairaj
in_english.meaning: Mairaj is a term used in Islam to describe the ascension of the Prophet Muhammad to heaven
in_english.long_meaning: Mairaj is a term used in Islam to describe the ascension of the Prophet Muhammad to heaven, where he was taken from the mosque al-Aqsa to the Garden of Eden and the heavens, as described in the Quran in Surah An-Najm. This event is one of the most important events in Islamic history and is considered a pivotal moment in the life of the Prophet Muhammad.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mairaj" is rooted in the rich Islamic culture and tradition. It reflects the belief in the ascension to heaven held by Muslims. This idea is mentioned in the Quran where it is stated that "Allah will say: This is the Day which Allah promised you in the former Scriptures -- the Day of the Great Command. On it are the Pilgrimage and the Festival, brought near to you in vision, from us: We make you see them in a divine opening." (Quran 7:145) The word 'Raj' or ascension is a significant part of Islamic eschatology, inspiring art, literature, and folktales.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Mairaj" signifies the ultimate devotion and yearning of every human soul for the divine presence of Allah. It represents a transformative journey from Earth, where we are currently physically confined, to the eternal realm of Allah's heaven. The Islamic belief in the Day of Judgment emphasizes this spiritual ascent of the soul, a journey that every individual will embark on after death, ultimately reuniting us with our Creator. This pursuit of nearness to Allah and the promise of an eternal life in the hereafter is the foundation of spiritual growth and seeking enlightenment in the Islamic faith.
